rationale: revertBits is a micro-benchmark dominated by tiny, hot, bit-manipulation kernels (ReverseBits32/64 at 61-87 bytes, ~1.1 KB total text), so the priority is transformations that obscure dataflow-level bitwise logic cheaply while penalizing anything that multiplies execution cost inside tight loops. SUB gets the strongest security/diversity weights with near-zero cost sensitivity because arithmetic/logic substitution is exactly suited to shift-mask-reverse kernels and its overhead is minimal; SPLIT is similarly cheap and enlarges the block inventory that makes SUB/IBR selections more effective on these few-block functions. FLA is favored as the primary structural defense (small functions flatten well and resist static recovery) but with a moderately high RuntimeCost weight so it is not applied to the hottest loops indiscriminately; BCF is kept available but heavily penalized on RuntimeCost and SizeCost because bogus-path execution in a benchmark's inner loop is the worst overhead/cost-benefit trade here. IBR receives moderate security weight with a mid-range runtime penalty as a secondary control-flow hardener. ICALL and IGV remain in consideration at reduced security weights since this program has only a handful of call sites (main -> ReverseBits*) and few globals, limiting their payoff. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low for the provably-safe local transforms (SUB, SPLIT) and moderate for control-flow rewrites, biasing selection toward transformations that preserve semantics on this strictly integer/branching workload.
